questions.q: Define irony and symbolism in your own words, giving one example of each from everyday life (not from the poem).
questions.a: Irony: saying "Great weather!" during a storm. Symbolism: a dove representing peace. A wrong answer (e.g., confusing irony with coincidence, or symbolism with metaphor) shows the student cannot distinguish the devices at a basic level.

questions.q: In the poem, the speaker says "Love is not love / Which alters when it alteration finds." Explain how this statement uses negation to define love. Why does the poet use so many negatives?
questions.a: The poet defines love by what it is not (not changeable, not bending) to emphasize its absolute constancy. Using negatives creates a strong, unshakeable definition. A wrong answer (e.g., "to make the poem rhyme") shows the student misses the rhetorical purpose of negation.

questions.q: Identify the symbol in the line "It is the star to every wandering bark." Explain what the star and the bark represent, and how this symbolism supports the theme.
questions.a: The star symbolizes true love as a fixed guide; the bark (ship) symbolizes a wandering soul. The symbolism shows love's constancy guiding the lost. A wrong answer (e.g., "star means hope") is vague and doesn't link to the poem's specific imagery.

questions.q: Analyze the irony in the final couplet: "If this be error, and upon me proved, / I never writ, nor no man ever loved." What type of irony is this, and what is its effect?
questions.a: This is verbal irony (paradox): the poet claims that if he's wrong, he never wrote (but he just did) and no one ever loved (but people do). It underscores his absolute certainty. A wrong answer (e.g., "it's dramatic irony") shows confusion between irony types.

questions.q: Evaluate the effectiveness of using Time as a personified figure with a "bending sickle's compass" as a symbol of mortality. How does this symbolism contrast with the symbol of the "ever-fixed mark"?
questions.a: Time's sickle symbolizes destructive, limited power; the ever-fixed mark symbolizes love's eternal, unchanging nature. The contrast heightens the theme. A weak answer merely describes the images without evaluating their thematic interplay.

questions.q: Write a four-line stanza (any rhyme scheme) that uses irony and symbolism to define a concept (e.g., friendship, courage, freedom) without naming it directly.
questions.a: A good stanza will use a symbol (e.g., a lighthouse for friendship) and irony (e.g., "It shines brightest when eyes are closed"). A poor attempt will lack either device or be too literal.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Irony is a literary device where the intended meaning of words is opposite to their literal meaning, or a ______ where the outcome is contrary to what is expected.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are ______ a poem that claims love never changes, yet the poet ends by saying if he's wrong, he never wrote and no one ever loved.
What is Irony? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Irony is a literary device where the intended meaning of words is opposite to their literal meaning, or a situation where the outcome is contrary to what is expected.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Irony?
questions.a: Students often think the final couplet is a literal statement (the poet really means he never wrote) rather than ironic hyperbole.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can identify and explain at least two instances of irony and two symbols in the poem, and articulate how they reinforce the theme of constancy of true love, using textual evidence in a structured PEEL paragraph.
